purpose: Bounded production replacement matrix: the mandatory workloads URM-native kernels must qualify against competitive upstream implementations before the next release. This is the acceptance envelope, not the expansion backlog. Cases, dtypes, tolerances, and performance budgets are frozen before tuning candidates; do not relax gates after seeing results.
comparator_policy: Each workload names a competitive upstream comparator frozen before independent confirmation. A slow reference implementation is never the sole performance baseline when a competitive compatible kernel exists. Comparisons include routing, layout conversion, allocation, dispatch, forward and backward, and cache/state updates; exclusions are declared per case.
measurement_policy: Report kernel/device execution, ordinary dispatch-inclusive invocation, and CUDA graph replay separately; graph replay never substitutes for ordinary-invocation qualification. Warm up compilation and autotuning, use synchronized paired randomized timing across multiple fresh processes, and report the slowdown confidence-interval bound against the frozen budget. Verdicts: qualified, correct_below_target, numeric_failed, inconclusive, unsupported.

hardware.notes: Validated line is torch 2.8.0 / triton 3.4.0 / CUDA 12.9. Re-qualification on a different runtime must re-freeze the environment record before comparing.
